study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Loreto et al., Alzheimer's & Dementia: Diagnosis, Assessment & Disease Monitoring, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Alzheimer's disease heterogeneity revealed by neuroanatomical normative modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Imperial APC clinical cohort; reference cohort pooled from publicly available datasets; adaptation dataset of CN adults scanned at ICHT (single site); ADNI reference cohort used for case-control comparisons.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The Imperial Amyloid PET Cohort (APC) was established at Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust (ICHT) in 2013 and includes all patients seen at the Imperial Memory Clinic..."; "The reference cohort consisted of a group of 33,072 cognitively normal adults pooled from publicly available neuroimaging datasets under a previous study"; "The adaptation dataset consisted of a group of 20 cognitively normal (CN) older adults who had an MRI scan at ICHT for research purposes."; "CN individuals from the ADNI reference cohort ( n = 79)"
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Loreto2024.pdf.md: 2 Methods / 2.1 Subjects; Loreto2024.pdf.md: 2.6 Statistical analysis / 2.6.1 Standard case-control comparisons

answer.Imperial APC: clinical AD cohort for applying normative model

answer.MULTI-DATASET (UNSPECIFIED OR N>=10): reference cohort for normative model training

answer.ADNI: CN control cohort for standard case-control comparisons

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: HBR normative model previously trained on the large reference cohort, then optimized with same-site CN controls (adaptation dataset) before applying to the Imperial APC clinical cohort; ADNI CN controls used for standard case-control comparison.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Hierarchical Bayesian regression was previously trained on the reference cohort..."; "This model was then optimized using cortical thickness data from controls scanned at the same acquisition site as the clinical cohort ( n = 20)."; "This recalibrated model was then used to generate regional cortical thickness z-scores for each participant in the clinical cohort"; "Cortical thickness extracted using FreeSurfer was compared between age- and sexmatched groups of patients from the Imperial APC clinical cohort ( n = 79) and CN individuals from the ADNI reference cohort ( n = 79)"
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Loreto2024.pdf.md: 2.3.2 Neuroanatomical normative modeling; Loreto2024.pdf.md: 2.6 Statistical analysis / 2.6.1 Standard case-control comparisons

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Reference cohort of healthy controls (n=33,072) used for pre-training; model optimized using same-site CN controls (adaptation dataset, n=20).
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The reference cohort consisted of a group of 33,072 cognitively normal adults pooled from publicly available neuroimaging datasets"; "Hierarchical Bayesian regression was previously trained on the reference cohort..."; "This model was then optimized using cortical thickness data from controls scanned at the same acquisition site as the clinical cohort ( n = 20)."
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Loreto2024.pdf.md: 2.1 Subjects; Loreto2024.pdf.md: 2.3.2 Neuroanatomical normative modeling

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Reference cohort age summary statistics were not reported; only a subset age range (49-87 years) is noted for participants matching the clinical cohort age range. Adaptation dataset age not reported.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "within this group, 17,586 (53.2%) participants were aged between 49 and 87 years, which was the age range in the clinical cohort studied."

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex breakdown for the reference cohort and adaptation dataset is not reported; sex is only mentioned as a covariate in the normative model.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: "Hierarchical Bayesian regression was previously trained on the reference cohort... using age and sex as the covariates"
